subject.title: Gateway becomes slow or times out under multi-session / multi-agent load

question: Should #92057 remain the canonical broad Gateway liveness tracker until a current-main large-state replay proves the reported Weixin/Codex multi-agent workload no longer stalls, or should maintainers split the remaining work now?
rationale: Source inspection shows partial mitigations, but the issue spans channel delivery, Gateway RPC handlers, event-loop health, session state, and compaction policy, so automation cannot safely decide the acceptance gate or scope boundary.

options.title: Keep canonical pending live replay
options.body: Keep this issue open until a sanitized current-main or latest-release replay shows status, stability, logs.tail, chat.history, sessions.list, sessions.compact, and channel delivery under the reported large-state workload.

options.title: Split to narrower blockers
options.body: Move raw transcript growth, default maintenance policy, and streaming/event-loop starvation to their narrower canonical issues and keep only a short tracking note here.

options.title: Close after maintainer override
options.body: Close only if maintainers accept the existing partial mitigations as sufficient without a large-state replay, acknowledging the remaining proof gap.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical pending live replay
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a sanitized current-main or latest-release replay shows status, stability, logs.tail, chat.history, sessions.list, sessions.compact, and channel delivery under the reported large-state workload.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent Gateway/session work makes this the best available owner for deciding whether the remaining scope stays broad or splits into narrower blockers.
